title: Cleaning chemicals for appliances: selection, compatibility and safe use
referencesAtStart: Official references for this lesson: Safe Work Australia, Preparing safety data sheets (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Using safety data sheets (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Managing the risks of hazardous chemicals in the workplace (model code of practice) (no date shown; publication date field blank).
audience: Workers who select, dilute, apply, store and dispose of detergents, degreasers, descalers and sanitisers used on specialty appliances
learningOutcomes: Select an approved cleaning product for an appliance and surface using the manufacturer's care instructions and the business product list
Explain the hazards of mixing incompatible cleaning chemicals, including acid with chlorine
Read a safety data sheet and label to identify the PPE, first aid and storage requirements for a product
Store, dilute and dispose of cleaning products without creating a new hazard

instruction.heading: Matching the product to the appliance and the surface
instruction.body: Specialty appliances are built from several materials at once: stainless steel panels, painted or powder-coated surfaces, plastics, rubber door seals, glass, membrane control panels and sometimes aluminium. A product that is safe on one of these can damage another. Alkaline degreasers remove cooking fat and oil but can attack some painted surfaces and some finishes if left on too long. Acid descalers remove mineral scale from water-carrying parts, but are not suitable for every metal or seal, and the manufacturer's instructions govern where they may be used. Chloride-containing products can damage some stainless steel finishes, and some rubber seals are damaged by strong solvents. Choose the product from the business's approved list for the appliance type, and check the manufacturer's care instructions for any product that is forbidden for that model. If the product you need is not on the list, do not substitute a product you have at home or in your van. Ask the supervisor to approve it, with its SDS, before use.

instruction.heading: Mixing hazards and what must never be combined
instruction.body: Never mix cleaning chemicals, and never use one product to 'boost' another. The most important combination to avoid is an acid with a chlorine-based product or bleach. Ammonia-based products must not be mixed with chlorine either. Alkaline products and acids can react strongly when mixed, producing heat and splash. Rinse the surface and the equipment between products, using the method set by the business, and leave a surface dry before changing to a product of a different type. Store products separately by type, so that an acid and a chlorine product are never next to each other on a shelf or in the van. Keep product in its original labelled container, and never decant an acid or a caustic into an unlabelled bottle.

instruction.heading: Reading the SDS and the label before you use a product
instruction.body: Every hazardous product must come with a safety data sheet, which sets out its hazards, the first aid steps, the PPE required, the storage and handling advice, and the disposal method. Read the SDS for each product before you use it for the first time, and keep it accessible in the vehicle or on the device. The label is the short version, and it must match the SDS. Check the signal words, the hazard statements, the dilution rate, the contact time and the PPE on the label. Follow the dilution rate and contact time exactly. A stronger solution does not clean faster and can cause corrosion, residue or injury. The Safe Work Australia model code on managing risks of hazardous chemicals covers safety data sheets and labelling.

procedure: Confirm the appliance type and the surface you will clean, and check the manufacturer's allowed and forbidden products.
Select a product from the business's approved list. If none fits, stop and ask the supervisor for approval with the SDS.
Check the SDS and the label, noting the PPE, the dilution rate, the contact time and the first aid steps.
Put on the PPE listed in the SDS and the business's required PPE field.
Dilute only to the label rate, using a clean measured container, and never mix two products in the same container or on the same cloth.
Apply the product to a cloth, not directly to the appliance, and keep it away from electrical parts, vents and seals.
Rinse by wiping with a clean damp cloth, dry the surface, and check it for residue before moving to the next product.
Store products separately by type, in labelled containers, and dispose of waste according to the SDS and the site's waste procedure.

workedExamples.situation: A commercial oven has a heavy grease build-up on the door glass. You have an alkaline oven cleaner in your van and a bottle of descaler for the coffee machine. You think the descaler will remove the grease faster.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which product do you use, and do you mix them?
workedExamples.reasoning: Do not mix the two, and do not use the descaler on the oven glass because it is not the right product for that job. Use the approved oven product from the business list at the label dilution. Keep the descaler separate and stored away from the oven product. If the grease cannot be removed with the approved product, record the surface, stop, and refer the glass question to the supervisor.

workedExamples.situation: Your bucket of sanitiser has been used for a dishwasher's exterior, and the next job requires a descaler. You think the bucket can be rinsed with the descaler solution to save time.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must happen between the two products?
workedExamples.reasoning: Empty the bucket, rinse it with clean water, and dry it before any new product is added. Never pour an acid into a bucket that held a chlorine-based sanitiser, because the residue can react and release gas. Label the new bucket and check the SDS for the descaler's PPE before you start.

equipmentAndPpe: Chemical-resistant gloves matched to the product in the SDS
Eye protection or face shield as set in the SDS
Labelled, clean measuring containers and spray bottles, one per product
Spill kit and the SDS for each product kept accessible on the vehicle or device
Ventilation as set by the SDS and the site, including opening a window or door where it is safe to do so

commonErrors.error: Using a product from home or the van that is not on the business list, because it looks suitable.
commonErrors.prevention: Use only products on the approved list, or get supervisor approval with the SDS before use.

commonErrors.error: Using a stronger dilution than the label, believing it will clean faster.
commonErrors.prevention: Dilute to the label rate and follow the contact time. A stronger solution can damage the surface and cause injury.

commonErrors.error: Rinsing a bucket of one product with another product, or storing an acid next to a chlorine product.
commonErrors.prevention: Rinse with clean water and dry between products. Store acids and chlorine products apart in labelled containers.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Never combine these products, and never use one to boost another. Safe Work Australia's SDS guidance says the SDS must be kept and easy to reach.
Safety data sheets and labels are required for hazardous chemicals, and makers and importers are responsible for SDS preparation, which should happen promptly after a chemical is brought in.
Waste water and disposal rules for cleaning chemicals depend on the state, the local council and the trade waste agreement. Do not tip chemical waste into stormwater drains.

qualityStandard: Each product used is on the business's approved list, or has supervisor approval with its SDS on file
Products are diluted to the label rate and used for the contact time on the label
No two products are mixed, and containers are rinsed and dried between products
documentationEvidence: The product name, batch or lot where shown, dilution used and the surface treated
The SDS reference for each product used on the job
Any spill, exposure or first aid event, with the action taken
summary: Choose products from the approved list and check the manufacturer's allowed and forbidden products.
Never mix products, and never combine acids with chlorine or bleach.
Read the SDS and label, dilute to the label rate, use the listed PPE, and store products apart.

knowledgeChecks.question: Why must an acid descaler never be used with a chlorine-based sanitiser or bleach?
options: The mixture can release chlorine gas, which is a serious inhalation hazard
The two products cancel each other out and leave a sticky residue
The mixture turns the surface blue, which is harmless but leaves a stain
The mixture only causes skin irritation, which is minor and clears quickly

knowledgeChecks.question: You want to use a product from home that is not on the business list. What should you do?
options: Use it if it looks suitable for stainless steel, since most household products are similar
Ask the supervisor for approval with the SDS before use, and use only an approved product until then
Use it on a small area first and say nothing to the supervisor about the product choice
Use it if the customer agrees to it, since the customer owns the product and the surface

knowledgeChecks.question: The label gives a dilution rate and a contact time. Which action is correct?
options: Use a stronger solution to save time on the job today
Use the product neat for heavy grease on the surface
Follow the dilution rate and the contact time on the label
Leave the product on until it dries, since that helps it work

knowledgeChecks.question: Where do you find the first aid steps and the PPE required for a cleaning product?
options: In the customer's appliance manual
In the hardware store's leaflet
In the cleaning cloth's packaging
In the product's safety data sheet

knowledgeChecks.question: Between two products, what is the correct method for a bucket or spray bottle?
options: Empty the container, rinse with clean water, and dry it before adding the new product
Add the new product on top of the old one, since they will combine safely in the same container
Shake it to mix the two products together, so the new product is evenly spread
Pour the old product into the new bottle, then top it up so the product is used well
